\-Gear lead times remain in excess of a year

\-This is being driven by big players submitting multi year POs

\-Concerns that the post COVID supply chain for Gear packages will never recover

- Find common points between same assembly types in different projects: What can we call “standard”, and can we take a manufacturing approach? (Having a stock of precut and labeled strut to specific lengths…this can be done in times of low workload. Cable tray widths are standard, as well as the “overhang” distances in our trapezes, so strut lengths are very standard as well) Research how more expensive could be to order the struts precut vs cutting in house.

\-Communication with manufacturers & distributers is critical for logistics flow to projects

\-Simply releasing all material is not the answer

- Space limitations
- Double handling
- Too much material too early

\-Cannot overlook logistics planning in pre construction

- Projects must game plan for material and prefab deliveries and follow the plan, rather than checking a box in the planning process

- Create BIM SOPs using input from the modelers that maintain highest productivity rates and are producing constant quality model/sheets.
- Revisit using Spools for assembly prefab drawings (Might be beneficial for items like Panels, transformers, duct bank sections, cable tray sections). Might be only possible to have the time for spooling, if we create the Prefab Designer position(s). The benefit will be more cleaner build drawings; having multiple drawings could allow for multiple teams to build assemblies at the same time (thinking of larger scale shop and work orders); 11x17 sheets that could be use for field install as well. Use Project Armor underground duct banks for case study.
- Do we have a constant QA/QC system and/or a person in our shop? Can we measure quality work in the shop and create a system for giving or taking points to the employees, and once a month recognize the best (might be giving a gift card).
- Do we collect feedback or ideas from the shop workers?
- When we are using a drill and need to use multiple tips for a work (inwall, panels), do they have to change the tips back and forth, or do they have multiple drills with the tips required?

\-Effective communication with manufacturers/suppliers is critical for delivery scheduling

Basic questions that require direct basic answers:

- What is showing up?
- When is it showing up?
- How will it show up?
- Who will unload, stock, and distribute it?

These are items that must regularly be updated in the on site logistics plan with field and office staff

The speaker touched on many potential impacts of a supply chain disruption.

- A pandemic, labor shortage, transportation, disruption, shut, downs, subcontractor bankruptcy, natural, disasters, etc.
  He stated to effectively manage these challenges it’s Crucial to proactively conduct a comprehensive CSI analysis on a project Of potential risks By trade and Develop contingency plans to mitigate their impact. From that we will find and determine:
- What items will create a day for day(critical) delay versus items that are non-critical
  What are the solutions to meeting these challenges?

Influences on project, visibility

• Material availability, transportation, logistics, and distance, all influence project viability.  Long transit times, supply chain bottlenecks, Or dependencies on single suppliers can expose projects to increase risk of scheduling delays.  Being proactive by diversify supplier networks, optimizing, transportation routes, or leveraging technology to enhance visibility and traceability access the supply chain. By understanding the interlay between these factors, Organizations can mitigate risk and ensure a steady flow of materials to support project objectives.

Lotte’s IWP Rhythm

\-Casey downloads the incurred hrs off coins into Trello every Mon or Tues.

\-On Thurs, we go over the trello board from start to finish

\-During going over Trello, we recognize pinch points,manpower,delays,upcoming activities along with equipment for the activities and material associated.

\-Also during this sit down, we look at budgeted hrs versus incurred hrs. This gives us a very good idea atleast half way through the IWP how we should do as far as hrs to save or hrs that will run over.

\-Also discuss the items that have been QAQC and new items that need to be. After they have been QAQC, then we close in coins 2 weeks later, just to make sure no more incurred time will hit these packages.

Redeemer IWP Rhythm

·        Discuss current BIM needs/dates/deadlines/feedback for work package layout with BIM coordinators, adjust applicable Trello cards accordingly

·        Work through due dates based on most recent scheduling information

·        Review “In Progress” IWPs card by card with respective superintendents/lead super/foremen, discuss time remaining until completion

·        Move completed work packages to QA/QC stage/column, make sure appropriate cards are attached

·        Move completed cards with QA/QC documentation attached to “Completed” column

·        Review “1 Week to Execution” IWPs card by card with supers/leads/foremen, move cards to “In Progress” as needed

·        Review “2 Weeks to Execution” IWPs, etc.

·        Review “3 Weeks to Execution” IWPS, etc.

·        Review “4 Weeks”

·        Review “5 Weeks”

·        Review “6 Weeks”

·        Review “Ready for Execution”

·        Review “IWP Backlog”

·        If necessary, discuss combining or splitting IWPs to more accurately capture work, coordinate with Russ to split budget accordingly

Pernod IWP Rhythm

- Look at items from the completed backwards
- Go over each card to check off any items
- Maneuver cards as necessary to accommodate current possible working scenarios.
- Discuss any questions or concerns on any of the packages as we go through them.
- Double check the schedule to each card and adjust to Scheduling
